title: The water cycle
examples: Teacher, what is the difference between evaporation and transpiration?
Can you show me a diagram of the whole water cycle?
Why does the water cycle happen?

explain.say: Say this word: evaporation. Evaporation is when liquid water turns into a gas called water vapour.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the water cycle. Look at the sun, the evaporation and the condensation. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Say this word: condensation. Condensation is when water vapour cools down and changes back into tiny liquid water droplets.
Say this word: precipitation. Precipitation is when the water falls back to Earth from the clouds. This can be rain or snow.
Say this word: collection. Collection is when the fallen water gathers in places like rivers and oceans.
Look at this picture. The water cycle shows how Earth's water moves around. It is a continuous process.
When you see steam rising from a hot puddle, you are seeing evaporation in action. The sun heats the water up.

faq.q: What is the difference between evaporation and transpiration?
faq.a: Evaporation is water turning into gas from surfaces like oceans. Transpiration is when plants release water vapour into the air through their leaves.
asks: Where does the water vapour come from?
Is plant water loss the same as evaporation?

faq.q: Do all the water cycle stages happen at the same time?
faq.a: No, they happen in sequence. The water must first evaporate before it can condense in the clouds.
asks: Can condensation happen without evaporation first?
Is there an order to the water cycle steps?

faq.q: What is the main source of energy for the water cycle?
faq.a: The main source of energy is the sun. The sun's heat provides the energy needed for evaporation to start.
asks: Does the sun power the water cycle?
What makes the water cycle move?

faq.q: Why is the water cycle important for life on Earth?
faq.a: It is important because it moves fresh water around the planet. This keeps rivers and lakes filled with water for us to use.
asks: What happens if the water cycle stops?
Does the water cycle give us drinking water?

faq.q: Can water cycle happen on other planets?
faq.a: It depends on the planet's atmosphere and temperature. Earth has the right conditions for this cycle to work well.
asks: Does the water cycle need liquid water?
Is the water cycle only for Earth?

facts: Evaporation changes liquid water into an invisible gas.
Condensation forms clouds when water vapour cools down.
Precipitation includes rain, snow, sleet, and hail.
Collection areas include oceans, lakes, and rivers.

quiz.say: Water vapour turning back into liquid droplets is called:
quiz.why: Condensation is the process where gas cools and turns back into liquid, like forming dew.

wrong.1: This is when liquid turns into gas, which is the opposite process.
wrong.2: This describes water falling from the sky, not the gas changing state.
wrong.3: This is where the water gathers, not the change of state itself.

quiz.say: When water falls from the sky as rain or snow, this is:
quiz.why: Precipitation is the term used for any form of water falling from the atmosphere to Earth.

wrong.0: Evaporation is the process of water going up into the air as gas.
wrong.1: Condensation is what happens in the clouds before the water falls.
wrong.2: Collection happens after the water lands in rivers or lakes.

quiz.say: Sun heats ocean water, turning it into vapour. This first step is:
quiz.why: The sun's heat energy causes the liquid water surface to change into a gas, which is evaporation.

wrong.0: Condensation happens later when the vapour cools down high in the sky.
wrong.1: Precipitation is the final step of the water falling back to Earth.
wrong.2: Collection is the final resting place for the water, not the initial change.
